propositions: A read-only audit of the rebar repository discovered 113 raw findings across 12 required concerns (code debt, architecture, tests, documentation, security, temporal decay) from a fixed snapshot, consolidating to 78 deduplicated candidates.

Independent verification against code, history, ADRs, and known-fine registry produced 47 survivors (29 critical, 18 major) with validity ≥0.75 and impact ≥0.5; 31 candidates were dropped as intentional, misread, immaterial, vague, or superseded.

Phase 3 produced 37 ordered remediation items (RP01–RP37) with two asymmetric-evidence proposals per survivor; Phase 4 approval decisions resolved or deferred all items: 9 approved for Janitor Cleanup ticketization, 3 absorbed into existing epics, 4 deferred to future passes, and 2 rejected.

Approved tickets include fsck repair pipeline staging, bidirectional config-surface enrollment, behavioral single-invocation oracle, MCP handshake extraction, Docker boundary testing, and Jira family link canonicalizer; rejected items include unified lifecycle contracts, package namespace relocation, and wire-dialect resolver.

No production code, tests, configuration, or documentation outside .joe-janitor/ and the tracker were modified; durable audit record, reusable tool playbook, and remediation plan were persisted at established artifact location.
Maintainer added mandatory revisit trigger after financial-stoneware-brant merge completion to re-census and re-decide on RP11 installed-package-namespace relocation at that terminal SHA.
